editorial:
Imagine a quiet dinner at a restaurant that suddenly turns into a nightmare when the owner is shot dead right in front of everyone. That is how this gritty crime story kicks off. You get to follow Alex, who is caught in a messy spot because his brother, Paul, is the lawyer for the two main suspects. While the police try to piece together the puzzle, you also meet Steinar, a detective whose personal life is falling apart. He is dealing with a bad marriage and a lot of stress, making the whole mood feel heavy and real. It is not just a simple whodunit; it is a look at how one violent act can ripple through different people's lives.

What really works here is the slow-burn tension and the solid acting. You will feel the stress these characters are under, though some might find the pace a bit slow at the start. If you love moody mysteries that focus on character drama over big explosions, you will really dig this.
endingExplained: The mystery wraps up when the truth about the restaurant owner's death comes out. It turns out the hit was part of a bigger power struggle involving greed and betrayal. The tension between the suspects and the legal team reaches a breaking point, leading to a final confrontation. After the killers are identified and caught, Steinar finds some closure with his own struggles, though the emotional scars remain for everyone involved.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Nordic noir and complex police dramas.
similarMovies: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
